snip.s: DVT and Venous Thromboembolism (with Pulmonary Embolism)

snip.t: | Pulmonary embolism | Sudden pleuritic chest pain, tachypnoea, pleural rub; normal or low‑grade fever; CT‑PA shows filling defect | Disproportionate dyspnoea, risk factors (immobility, DVT); D‑dimer elevated, CXR often normal |

| Pulmonary embolism with infarction | Acute pleuritic chest pain, tachycardia, risk factors for thrombosis, wedge‑shaped opacity on CT | CT pulmonary angiography shows filling defect; no chronic mucus plugging or bronchial wall thickening. |
| Pulmonary embolism | Acute dyspnoea, pleuritic chest pain, tachycardia; risk factors for thrombosis | CT pulmonary angiography shows filling defects; D‑dimer elevation; no mass on imaging |

| Pulmonary embolism | Pleuritic chest pain, tachypnoea, pleuritic rub, risk factors (immobility, cancer), sinus tachycardia, D‑dimer ↑ | V/Q scan or CT pulmonary angiogram shows filling defect; right‑heart strain on ECG |
snip.s: Approach to Cardiovascular Symptoms and Examination

snip.t: | CT Pulmonary Angiogram | Pulmonary embolism, chronic thromboembolic disease, lung parenchyma | Filling defects (PE), web/bands (CTEPH), interstitial lung disease |
